title: The Umbrella Strategy
scene: You check the weather forecast before leaving home and decide that a thirty per cent chance of rain is low enough to leave your umbrella behind. When it rains anyway, you slowly realise the forecast was not the problem; your interpretation was.
sceneJa: 降水確率30％を見て傘を置いて出る。雨が降り始めてから、予報が間違っていたのではなく、自分が都合よく解釈していただけだと気づく。

chunks.ja: 天気予報を確認しました
家を出る前に
すると〜と出ていました

chunks.en: a thirty per cent chance of rain.
chunks.ja: 降水確率30％だと

chunks.en: Thirty per cent sounded low enough
chunks.ja: 30％なら十分低そうに聞こえて
傘を置いていくには
特に傘を持ち歩くことは
いつも少し悲観的に感じるので
昼になると
空が曇ってきました
それでも信じることにしました
統計的なプロセスを
5分後
雨が降り始めました
見事なまでの自信を持って

chunks.en: I stood under a shop awning
chunks.ja: 私は店のひさしの下に立ちました
ほかの3人と一緒に
どうやら彼らもしていたようです
同じような数学的判断を

chunks.en: One of them checked his phone
chunks.ja: そのうちの一人がスマホを確認し

chunks.en: and announced that the chance of rain
chunks.ja: 降水確率が〜だと知らせました
今や90％になっていると
それは正確でした
ただ、それほど役には立ちませんでした

chunks.en: given that we were already watching it happen.
chunks.ja: すでに目の前で雨が降っていることを考えると
10分後
待つのを諦め
駅まで走りました

chunks.en: using my bag as an extremely poor umbrella.
chunks.ja: バッグを非常に性能の悪い傘として使いながら
着くころには
シャツも濡れ
靴も濡れ

chunks.en: and the contents of my bag had developed their own weather system.
chunks.ja: バッグの中には独自の気象システムまで発達していました

chunks.en: The forecast had never actually said
chunks.ja: 天気予報は実際には一度も言っていませんでした
雨が降らないとは

chunks.en: I had simply translated ‘thirty per cent’
chunks.ja: 私はただ『30％』を翻訳していただけでした
『自分には関係ない』と
だから厳密に言えば
天気予報は正しかったのです
それは少し安心できました

chunks.en: because at least one of us had understood the forecast.
chunks.ja: 少なくとも私たちのうち片方は予報を理解していたので

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: Thirty per cent sounded low enough / to leave my umbrella behind
Thirty per cent / sounded low / enough to leave my umbrella
Thirty / per cent sounded / low enough to leave
questions.explanation: ‘Sounded low enough’ forms the judgment, and the to-infinitive explains what it seemed low enough to do.

questions.question: What does ‘given that’ mean here?
options: In spite of the fact that
questions.explanation: ‘Given that’ introduces a fact that makes the previous statement easier to understand or evaluate.

questions.question: Why is the final line funny?
options: The speaker thinks the forecast and the rain were both wrong
The speaker admits that the forecast understood the situation better than he did
The speaker believes thirty per cent means it cannot rain
questions.explanation: The speaker dryly treats the forecast as if it were the other person in the conversation, admitting that only one of them understood what thirty per cent really meant.

speak: Start calm and slightly self-satisfied, as if the umbrella decision is perfectly rational. Keep ‘with impressive confidence’ dry rather than dramatic. Pause before ‘So technically,’ and deliver the last sentence almost as a sincere consolation; the joke works because the speaker quietly admits defeat.
review: Today’s flow: forecast → confident interpretation → evidence changes → inconvenience → reinterpretation → dry admission. Notice the difference between what information actually says and what we want it to mean.
